scope.summary: Prove every automation surface (command contract, macros, batch runner, data-driven graphics, find/change, plugin surface, inspect/codegen, asset/OS/clipboard handoff) is operable from BOTH the native operator UI and the typed model/plugin surface, honors the headless/quiet law for all background/batch execution, exposes stable AccessKit/author_id targets + structured state to Argus so a no-context model can drive and re-observe every automation control, and is documented in the dual-audience Studio UserManual with operator workflows + model/plugin command reference derived from the command inputSchemas.
acceptance_criteria: every automation surface dual-operable, quiet-law-honoring, Argus-visible, manual-covered
proof_targets: automation Argus coverage + dual-operability + manual self-consistency
expected_tests: argus: every automation control reachable + re-observable by author_id
test: dual-operability (UI + model surface) for each automation surface
HBR-MAN-003: every automation command_id has a manual entry

risk_if_missed: Automation surfaces not model-discoverable/steerable or undocumented; no-context models blocked.

risks: Scaffold-only claim without runtime proof (Spec-Realism Gate).
Domain MT forking a canonical primitive instead of referencing 14.23.
PostgreSQL/SQLite creep or a write that bypasses the typed SurrealDB boundary on a studio_* authority path.
minimum_controls: At least one proof command exercises executable runtime or a Handshake-managed resource boundary.
Reference canonical primitives (14.23); no shadow primitives.
no_legacy_database_tripwire plus typed-SurrealDB-boundary proof on every authority write.
